title: Practitioner Exam
description: 40 questions drawn at random from a pool of 60, covering Pentaho 11 installation, components, ports, prerequisites, post-install tasks, upgrades and client tools. Pass mark is 80%. Open-book — browse any module to refresh your memory or ask the AI assistant for help. Your answers are saved as you go, so leaving the page to look something up is fine. Explanations show after submission so you can learn from any answers you missed.

questions.scenario: An estate runs Pentaho Server 10.2. A team wants to roll the PDI 11.0 client out to its developers now and leave the server upgrade until next quarter.
questions.prompt: What is the problem with that plan?
options: The 11.0 client cannot open transformations that were saved in 10.2.
None: the client negotiates a protocol with whichever server version it meets.
The 11.0 client must first be registered as a plugin on the 10.2 server.
Client and server should run the same version, so 11.0 against 10.2 is unsupported.
questions.explanation: The PDI client and the Pentaho Server are released and supported as a **matched pair**, so an 11.0 client against a 10.2 server is a combination nobody has certified, and the client does not negotiate its way across versions.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Overview — What's New

questions.scenario: A platform team wants to install Pentaho 11.0 on a standard Linux image that is not listed in the Pentaho 11.0 Components Reference. They say the archive will start on it, and they are probably right.
questions.prompt: What is the strongest argument for requesting an exception from the team?
options: The License Manager will not activate on an unlisted image.
Support covers tested configurations, not ones that merely start.
An unlisted image stops the archive from unpacking at all.
The Plugin Manager installs plugins only on listed images.
questions.explanation:
A supported matrix is not a statement regarding whether the software functions; it defines the specific configurations that the vendor has tested and will **support**. Systems outside of these listed configurations risk having a support case declined during a service outage.

Because the archive is a ZIP file, it can be unpacked and started on almost any system, which means the ability to start does not equate to a **tested configuration**.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Overview — Components Reference

questions.scenario: A customer downloads the Pentaho 11.0 GA binaries from the Customer Portal and installs the server on a networked host. The server starts, but no license is detected.
questions.prompt: What does the administrator need to supply?
options: An offline licence, which every new server requires first
The trial licence file from the public 30-day download
Nothing, since the GA binaries carry a 30-day trial licence
An Activation ID or licensing URL, entered in the License Manager
questions.explanation: GA binaries from the Customer Portal are activated with an **Activation ID** or the customer's licensing URL, entered through **Administration > Licenses**.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Getting Started — Support Portal & Licensing

questions.scenario: The `PENTAHO_JAVA_HOME` variable was never set on a Pentaho 11 host. Following an OS patch cycle, the server fails to start and the default `java` command reports OpenJDK 17.
questions.prompt: What is the correct fix?
options: Install Java 21 and set `PENTAHO_JAVA_HOME` to it
Downgrade to Java 11, the long-term baseline
Add a flag in `server.xml` so Tomcat accepts Java 17
Move the repository to PostgreSQL 17 and restart
questions.explanation: Pentaho 11 is certified on **Java 21**. Because the `PENTAHO_JAVA_HOME` variable was not set, the server executed the system default of Java 17 after the patch. Setting `PENTAHO_JAVA_HOME` pins the server to the specific **JVM** required for compatibility, ensuring that subsequent system updates do not change the underlying Java environment.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Prepare Environment

questions.scenario: The build plan requires PostgreSQL 17 for the repository, but the `apt install postgresql` command on Ubuntu 24.04 installs version 16 from the distribution's own repository.
questions.prompt: How should the installer obtain version 17?
options: Keep 16 and set a version 17 compatibility level in postgresql.conf
Wait for Ubuntu 24.04's own repository to move to version 17
Add the PostgreSQL project's apt repository and install postgresql-17
Build PostgreSQL 17 from source and install it by hand
questions.explanation:
The installer must add the **PostgreSQL Global Development Group (PGDG)** repository to provide access to the specific version required.

By adding this repository, the installer can target the specific package `postgresql-17`, which is maintained and patched through the standard **apt** package manager.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Prepare Environment

questions.scenario: A host currently runs another Java application listening on port 8080, and the new Pentaho Server fails to start on that port.
questions.prompt: What must be changed so that both applications can run?
options: The AJP connector port in `server.xml`, leaving the HTTP one alone
The repository database port, which also defaults to 8080
Tomcat's shutdown port in `server.xml`, which Tomcat binds before HTTP
The HTTP connector port in `server.xml`, and the server URL to match
questions.explanation:
When the **HTTP connector port** in `server.xml` is changed from the default to avoid a conflict, the `fully-qualified-server-url` in `server.properties` must be updated to match the new port.

This ensures that the links generated by the server are correct and point to the new location.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.scenario: The installation creates a dedicated `pentaho` account that owns /opt/pentaho and runs the server. A colleague encounters permission errors during setup and proposes running the entire environment as root.
questions.prompt: How should that proposal be judged?
options: Reject it, but only because the Upgrade Installer needs pentaho-owned files
Accept it, because Tomcat drops root privileges once it has started
Reject it: any flaw in the server would run with full control of the host
Accept it for setup only, then fix ownership afterwards at no risk
questions.explanation:
The server is a network-facing JVM, so the account it runs as sets how far an attacker can reach through a flaw in it. A dedicated non-root owner limits that **blast radius**, and setting ownership correctly once is what ends the permission errors.

Running as root, even only during setup, leaves root-owned files the `pentaho` account cannot write.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Prepare Environment

questions.scenario: A systemd unit and several scripts on a new host must find the Pentaho install root, `/opt/pentaho`, without hard-coding it. The value must be available to every user after a reboot.
questions.prompt: Where should `PENTAHO_BASE` be defined?
options: With export in the current shell
In the pentaho user's ~/.bashrc
In Tomcat's conf/server.xml
In /etc/environment
questions.explanation: Defining the variable in `/etc/environment` ensures that it is **read at every login** and can be loaded by systemd units via the `EnvironmentFile` directive. This configuration ensures that every user and the service see the same value after a reboot.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Prepare Environment

questions.scenario: A nightly cron entry must run a `.kjb` that runs three transformations in sequence and stops if one fails, on a host with no desktop.
questions.prompt: Which command-line tool should the cron entry call?
options: Pan
Spoon
Carte
Kitchen
questions.explanation:
The **Kitchen** command-line tool is used to execute jobs, including those that require complex logic such as sequencing and error handling.

It provides the necessary functionality to execute a .kjb file from a headless environment.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Getting Started — Components (Pan / Kitchen)

questions.scenario: An ETL team wants transformations sent from its design tools to run on two dedicated worker machines, with a browser page to watch them and a REST API for its scheduler.
questions.prompt: Which component runs on the worker machines?
options: Carte
Pentaho User Console
Kitchen
Pan
questions.explanation: The **Carte** component is a lightweight Jetty-based server that runs transformations and jobs sent to it remotely, supports clustering, and exposes a status page and a REST API.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Getting Started — Components (Carte)

questions.scenario: A node is being built specifically to run scheduled ETL, and no reports or dashboards will ever be served from it. A colleague wants the full analytics plugin set installed to ensure every server in the estate is identical.
questions.prompt: How should that request be judged?
options: Leave them off, and copy any plugin it does need in by hand
Install them all: the server cannot start without the analytics set
Leave Analyzer and Dashboard Designer off: cost here with no use
Install them all: unused plugins cost nothing until someone opens them
questions.explanation:
**Analyzer** and **Dashboard Designer** serve interactive analytics; a node that serves no users does not benefit from these features but does incur a cost in memory and a larger attack surface.

Plugins load when the server starts, so unused plugins are not free. The server does not require the analytics plugins to start.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Server Plugins

questions.scenario: After a disk failure, an administrator restores only the jackrabbit database from backup. Reports and folders are back in the User Console, but every schedule has gone.
questions.prompt: What was left out of the restore?
options: The hibernate database, which holds the schedules
The pentaho-solutions folder, which holds schedule files
The quartz database, which holds the scheduler's data
The opsmart database, which holds scheduled job definitions
questions.explanation: The **Quartz** database holds the scheduler's data. While the Jackrabbit database contains content, security, and metadata, it does not contain the data necessary to maintain scheduled jobs.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Install Pentaho Server (Repository)

questions.scenario: A security review reports that the Pentaho Server discloses the Tomcat version to anyone who makes an HTTP request.
questions.prompt: What removes that disclosure?
options: Switch the HTTP connector to AJP, which sends no such header
Delete the Tomcat version file from the server's lib directory, then restart
Change the shutdown port to an unpredictable value
Set the server attribute on the connector in server.xml, then restart
questions.explanation: By default, Tomcat includes version information in the **Server header**. Configuring the `server` attribute on the connector within the `server.xml` file overrides this default behavior and removes the version disclosure upon a server restart.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Post Installation Tasks

questions.scenario: To harden a server, an administrator sets `port="-1"` on the Server element in Tomcat's `server.xml`. The server still starts, but stopping it through its systemd unit, which runs `stop-pentaho.sh`, now hangs until the unit's timeout.
questions.prompt: Why does stopping hang?
options: The stop script reaches Tomcat through that port, which is now closed.
The shutdown command must now be sent over HTTPS instead.
systemd relies on the shutdown port to track the server's main process.
Port -1 disables the HTTP connector, so requests cannot drain.
questions.explanation: The `stop-pentaho.sh` script attempts to stop the service by sending the shutdown command to the local port specified in the configuration. When the port is set to -1, that **shutdown listener** is disabled, meaning the script cannot communicate with Tomcat to initiate a graceful shutdown, causing the systemd unit to wait until it reaches its timeout.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Post Installation Tasks

questions.scenario: An estate running Pentaho 7.1 is to be upgraded to 10.1, and the plan is to point the Pentaho Upgrade Installer straight at it.
questions.prompt: What is wrong with the plan?
options: The installer starts from 8.3, so 7.1 must first reach 8.3
The installer upgrades only the client tools, not the server
Nothing: the installer upgrades any release from 7.0 up
No upgrade path exists, so 7.1 must be reinstalled
questions.explanation:
The **Pentaho Upgrade Installer** only supports versions from 8.3 or later. Because the current environment is on 7.1, the system must first be upgraded to at least 8.3 before the installer can be used to reach version 10.1.

The installer does not accept any releases prior to 8.3 and is designed to upgrade both the Pentaho Server and the client tools simultaneously.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Pentaho Upgrade & Patches

questions.scenario: A host has 15 GB free on the Pentaho filesystem and the upgrade window is booked. A colleague proposes starting on time and clearing space if the Upgrade Installer complains.
questions.prompt: How should that be judged?
options: Reject it: the installer needs 22 GB, so free it before the window
Reject it: copy the new files over the old ones instead
Accept it: its backup of the products can be skipped for space
Accept it: 15 GB is well above what the installer needs
questions.explanation:
The **Upgrade Installer** requires a minimum of 22 GB of free space to proceed. Because the installer also creates a backup of the existing products before performing the upgrade, the required space must be available before the window begins rather than being secured during the process.

Providing only 15 GB of space is insufficient to meet the **minimum requirements** for the installation to complete successfully.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Pentaho Upgrade & Patches

questions.scenario: Design tools must be deployed onto a fleet of Linux workstations where the desktop team determines the specific directory locations for every file.
questions.prompt: Which installation route fits?
options: The PDI Plugin Manager on each workstation
The Business Analytics Evaluation Wizard
A manual install from each tool's ZIP
A Pentaho Server on each workstation
questions.explanation: A manual installation from the per-tool ZIP files allows for installation on Linux systems and ensures the files are placed exactly where the build requires them. This approach provides the necessary control over the **file paths** and directory structure required by the desktop team.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Install Client Tools — Client Plugins

questions.scenario: A MySQL driver is distributed into the Pentaho Server's `tomcat/lib` folder, and reports on the server connect to MySQL. On a designer's workstation, Spoon fails to connect to the same database with a driver error.
questions.prompt: What is the cause?
options: The driver has to be registered through the License Manager.
Spoon cannot connect to MySQL; only the server can.
Spoon borrows the server's drivers, so the server needs restarting first.
Each client tool loads drivers from its own folder, which lacks the JAR.
questions.explanation:
Each client tool, such as Spoon, loads **JDBC drivers** from its own local directory rather than sharing the libraries used by the Pentaho Server.

Because the server and the client tools are separate environments, the JAR must be placed in the specific folder used by the client tool for a successful connection.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Install Client Tools — Client Plugins

questions.scenario: An engineer places a PDI plugin into the plugins directory manually because it is faster than using the Plugin Manager.
questions.prompt: What is the consequence of this action?
options: PDI refuses to start until the plugin is registered.
It will not show in the Plugin Manager, so updates and removal remain manual.
The Plugin Manager deletes the file the next time it runs.
Nothing: the Plugin Manager adopts whatever it finds in the plugins folder.
questions.explanation:
Because the plugin was not installed via the **Plugin Manager** interface, the application does not register it within the management system. While the plugin remains functional, it will not be listed for updates or removal through the standard UI.

This creates a situation where the plugin becomes a **manual management** task, as the system does not automatically adopt or track files placed in the directory outside of the official installation path.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Install Client Tools — Kettle Plugins

questions.scenario: A plugin has just been installed through the Plugin Manager, and the manager reported success. However, the new steps are not appearing in the PDI client.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely reason?
options: Plugins installed through PUC never reach the PDI client
Neither the server nor the PDI client has been restarted since
The plugin must also be copied into the plugins folder by hand
New steps appear only after the license has been refreshed
questions.explanation: A newly installed plugin is not active until both the Pentaho Server and the PDI client are **restarted**. After that, its steps appear, and its version can be checked in **Tools > Plugin Manager**.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Install Client Tools — Kettle Plugins

questions.scenario: A team of ETL developers works on locked-down laptops where every desktop installation requires a change request. They must build and edit transformations and jobs against the Pentaho 11.0 server they already run.
questions.prompt: Which 11.0 capability fits best?
options: The redesigned User Console, which replaces Spoon for ETL design
Pipeline Designer, which authors transformations and jobs in the browser
Semantic Model Editor, which builds transformations and jobs in the browser
Carte, which serves a browser canvas for designing jobs
questions.explanation: The **Pipeline Designer** allows users to author transformations and jobs directly in a web browser. This capability maintains compatibility with designs made in Spoon, allowing developers to work on restricted hardware without requiring a local installation.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Overview — What's New

questions.scenario: An estate upgrading to PDI 11.0 previously used a separate big data add-on distribution in addition to the standard client. The build engineer cannot find a separate big data distribution for version 11.0.
questions.prompt: Why is the separate distribution missing?
options: 11.0 delivers big data components as plugins, like any other.
The big data distribution ships a quarter after each release.
Big data components now ship inside the Pentaho Server install only.
11.0 dropped big data support from PDI altogether.
questions.explanation: Since PDI 11.0 removed Karaf and OSGi, it no longer requires a separate distribution for big data. These components are now delivered as **plugins**, which are deployed in the same manner as other PDI plugins, and both the client and the server were reduced by more than 1 GB.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Overview — What's New

questions.scenario: An architect is planning a production rollout of Pentaho 11.0 for 400 business users. A stakeholder wants every user moved to the redesigned Pentaho User Console on day one.
questions.prompt: What is the soundest position?
options: Move everyone, since the redesign replaced the old console in 11.0
Keep the old console, since the redesign has no login page yet
Keep the existing console as the default, since the redesign is a preview
Move everyone, since the old console goes at the first 11.0 patch
questions.explanation: The redesigned console is a **preview** in version 11.0 where the behavior and interface may still change. The existing console remains available until the two reach feature parity, making the original console the safer choice for a production rollout.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Overview — What's New

questions.scenario: A company standardizes on Okta for single sign-on and wants its users to reach the Pentaho 11.0 User Console with their Okta login.
questions.prompt: What does 11.0 offer for this?
options: An LDAP bridge that Okta has to emulate for Pentaho
Built-in OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 authentication
Only a custom Spring Security module written in-house
Single sign-on through Carte's REST API
questions.explanation: Pentaho 11.0 supports **OpenID Connect** and **OAuth 2.0** for the Pentaho Server. This provides native single sign-on with any OIDC-compliant identity provider, such as Okta, Azure, or Google.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Overview — What's New

questions.scenario: In a Pentaho 10.2 estate, administrators were unable to allow one group to use Analyzer while blocking another plugin because Read Content opened content from any plugin. The estate is migrating to version 11.0.
questions.prompt: What does 11.0 change for this requirement?
options: Folder permissions that now decide which plugins open
A per-user switch in each plugin's own configuration file
Finer-grained permissions that allow or block individual plugins
Nothing, since plugin access is still governed by Read Content
questions.explanation: Version 11.0 introduces **finer-grained permissions** to the Pentaho Server. These permissions allow administrators to specifically allow or block individual plugins, providing more granular control over data sources and execution than the previous Read Content limitation.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Overview — What's New

questions.scenario: An operations team wants to run Pentaho 11.0 on Amazon EKS, supplying its license and configuration files when a container starts rather than baking them into a custom image.
questions.prompt: What does 11.0 provide for this?
options: A Carte cluster image that carries the license server
Only the archive install, which the team must containerize itself
A build step that rebakes the image around each new license
Prebuilt images whose entrypoint scripts take runtime overrides
questions.explanation: Pentaho 11.0 provides **prebuilt images** for various container environments, including Amazon EKS. These images utilize **entrypoint scripts** that allow for runtime overrides of configuration files and licenses, eliminating the need to bake these specific files into the image during the build process.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Overview — What's New

questions.scenario: A platform team already collects traces and metrics from its services in Datadog. It wants PDI runs to appear there too, with task timings and the execution hierarchy.
questions.prompt: What is the Pentaho 11.0 route?
options: The OpenTelemetry plugin, exporting logs, traces and metrics
Carte's status page, scraped on a schedule
The Operations Mart, read by a database agent
Parsing Kitchen's console output and forwarding it to Datadog
questions.explanation: The **OpenTelemetry plugin** sends hierarchical logs, traces with task timing and execution hierarchy, and metrics in an open format that Datadog, Splunk, Elastic, and other providers can consume.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Overview — What's New

questions.scenario: Modelers building Analyzer cubes on Pentaho 11.0 want a web-based modeling workflow that also opens the Mondrian models they already have.
questions.prompt: Which tool fits?
options: Schema Workbench
Semantic Model Editor
Metadata Editor
Aggregation Designer
questions.explanation: The **Semantic Model Editor** is a tool introduced in version 11.0 that allows users to build and manage Mondrian models directly in a web browser. It specifically supports both new and existing Mondrian models within this web-based workflow.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Overview — What's New

questions.scenario: A firewall request for a new single-host Pentaho Server must list the ports users' browsers need. The repository database runs on the same host.
questions.prompt: Which port must be open to users?
options: 8012, the server's shutdown port
8080, Tomcat's HTTP port
9001, the HSQL sample database's port
5432, the repository database's port
questions.explanation: Users reach the User Console over **Tomcat's HTTP port**, which is 8080 by default.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.scenario: A developer schedules a transformation from Spoon on the Pentaho Server, but the transformation is saved as a .ktr file on their local laptop. The scheduled run cannot find the file.
questions.prompt: What has the developer missed?
options: Scheduling from Spoon needs Carte running on the laptop
Scheduled work must be stored in the Pentaho Repository
The laptop's kettle.properties must be copied to the server
The server can schedule jobs only, never transformations
questions.explanation:
The scheduler hands work to the server's Quartz scheduler. Because the server cannot access local files on a workstation, scheduled work must be stored in the **Pentaho Repository** to be accessible by the server.

When a transformation is stored in the repository, the server can locate and execute it independently of the developer's local environment.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.scenario: A customer's database team supports only Microsoft SQL Server and Oracle, and will not run PostgreSQL.
questions.prompt: Can that team host the Pentaho Repository?
options: Only on Oracle, whose XML types the repository's schema requires
Only once the repository is moved into an embedded H2 file
No: the repository requires PostgreSQL in Pentaho 11
Yes: the repository can sit on SQL Server or Oracle too
questions.explanation:
The **Pentaho Repository** is backed by Apache Jackrabbit and supports several relational database engines, including PostgreSQL, SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, and MariaDB.

While PostgreSQL is the recommended default, it is not a requirement for the repository to function. The repository does not rely on specific features like Oracle's XML types for its schema.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.scenario: Business users must see Customer and Order Total in their Interactive Reports rather than table and column names. Certain users must only see rows belonging to their specific region.
questions.prompt: Which client tool defines that business layer?
options: Metadata Editor
Report Designer
Aggregation Designer
Schema Workbench
questions.explanation: The **Metadata Editor** is used to build the business models behind Interactive Reports. This tool defines the business layer by establishing friendly names, relationships, and security constraints at the model level.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.scenario: Analyzer reports over a 400-million-row fact table take several minutes to open at the year and quarter levels, although the cube itself is well designed.
questions.prompt: Which tool addresses this most directly?
options: Schema Workbench, to rename the Time hierarchy's levels
Carte, to spread the Analyzer query over worker nodes
Aggregation Designer, to build aggregate tables for those levels
Metadata Editor, to add year and quarter as business columns
questions.explanation: The **Aggregation Designer** identifies and builds aggregate tables so that queries at coarse levels, such as year and quarter, read a summary instead of scanning 400 million rows of raw data.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.scenario: Nightly loads on one PDI server now overrun their window. The transformations are CPU-bound and split cleanly by region, and an architect is weighing options.
questions.prompt: Which option addresses the bottleneck?
options: Spread the regions across machines on a Carte cluster
Switch the loads from Kitchen to Pan to cut the job overhead
Raise the Pentaho Server's Tomcat thread count
Move the repository database onto the PDI server itself
questions.explanation: A **Carte cluster** spreads CPU-bound work that partitions cleanly, such as by region, over several machines, which is what a saturated single server needs.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Getting Started — Components (Carte)

questions.scenario: A security scan of a production Pentaho Server finds port 9001 listening, and no one on the team knows why.
questions.prompt: What does this finding most likely indicate?
options: Carte is listening there for remote transformations.
The shutdown port was moved to 9001 during the install.
PostgreSQL has been bound to a second port by mistake.
The HSQL sample database still starts, so the samples remain.
questions.explanation:
Port 9001 is the default port for the **HSQL database** engine. This server starts automatically if the sample data definitions remain in the web application's `web.xml` file.

Removing the sample data from the configuration before deploying to a production environment will prevent the **HSQL server** from starting on that port.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Getting Started — Components

questions.scenario: A customer runs a hardened, centrally patched Tomcat estate and requires Pentaho to be deployed into this environment rather than alongside a second, bundled Tomcat.
questions.prompt: Is the archive installation the right route?
options: No: Pentaho 11.0 cannot run inside a customer's own Tomcat at all.
Yes: the archive deploys into any existing Tomcat.
Yes: the archive is the only route supported for 11.0.
No: the archive brings its own Tomcat, so a manual install fits.
questions.explanation:
The **archive installation** ships Pentaho with its own bundled Tomcat instance, which is suitable for environments where a pre-existing server is not available.

When a customer already provides an application server, a **manual installation** is required to deploy Pentaho into the existing environment.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Overview

questions.scenario: An administrator adds `PENTAHO_JAVA_HOME` to `/etc/environment` and, in the same terminal session, runs `echo $PENTAHO_JAVA_HOME`, which prints nothing.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely reason?
options: `/etc/environment` accepts only variables that begin with `JAVA_`.
Each line in `/etc/environment` needs `export` in front of it.
Only root sessions are allowed to read `/etc/environment`.
The file is read at login, so re-login or source it.
questions.explanation:
The system reads the `/etc/environment` file only when a **new session** starts. A shell that is already open does not see the changes until the session is restarted or the file is manually sourced.

Any variable name is allowed in this file, and the system accepts plain `NAME=value` lines without the `export` command.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Prepare Environment

questions.scenario: An Ubuntu host has both OpenJDK 17 and OpenJDK 21 installed, and the command `java -version` reports 17.
questions.prompt: Which command makes 21 the system's default java?
options: sudo update-alternatives --config java
sudo systemctl set-default java-21
export JAVA_VERSION=21
sudo apt install --default openjdk-21-jdk
questions.explanation: The `update-alternatives` command is used to manage the **alternatives** available to the system. Using the `--config` flag allows the administrator to select which installed Java version the `java` command points to on a system-wide basis.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Prepare Environment

questions.scenario: The installation procedure grants the `pentaho` database role SUPERUSER to make creating the repository databases simple. The same script is about to be run for production.
questions.prompt: How should that step be judged for production?
options: Replace it with least-privilege roles; SUPERUSER is for a demo.
Keep it, since the server needs SUPERUSER to start.
Drop the role and let the server connect as postgres.
Keep it, but change the role's password once the install is done.
questions.explanation: A permanent superuser for application use gives anything that compromises it control of the whole database server. Production environments require **least-privilege roles** that hold only the permissions required for operation, as the original procedure intended to elevate privileges only to simplify a demo.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Prepare Environment

questions.scenario: The Pentaho Server is moved to a different host from its PostgreSQL repository. The server cannot connect to the database, even though the PostgreSQL service is running and `pg_hba.conf` allows the server's IP address.
questions.prompt: What other configuration must be updated on the database host?
options: The port set in `pg_hba.conf`, which defaults to 5433
`shared_buffers` in `postgresql.conf`, which blocks remote connections
`listen_addresses` in `postgresql.conf`, which defaults to local only
The JDBC driver in the database host's lib folder
questions.explanation: By default, PostgreSQL accepts only local connections, so `listen_addresses` in `postgresql.conf` must name the interface the server will reach, or `*` for all of them. A **restart** follows, plus any firewall rule for port 5432.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Prepare Environment

questions.scenario: The `pg_hba.conf` file is updated from `md5` to `scram-sha-256`. The Pentaho Server can no longer authenticate to the repository, even though `psql` logins with the same credentials still succeed.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely cause?
options: SCRAM requires the repository to move to another port.
The server's PostgreSQL JDBC driver is too old for SCRAM.
scram-sha-256 applies only to the postgres superuser.
psql caches its credentials, hiding the same failure.
questions.explanation: The **JDBC driver** used by the Pentaho Server must support the `scram-sha-256` authentication method. While the `psql` utility uses its own internal library that supports SCRAM, an outdated driver in the application server will fail to authenticate when the method is changed.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Prepare Environment

questions.scenario: Administrators want reports of which content users run and how it performs, but the `pentaho_mart` scripts were skipped when the repository was created.
questions.prompt: Which part of the repository is missing?
options: The Operations Mart, which holds usage and performance data
The Tomcat access log, which the server's usage reports read
Jackrabbit, which logs every content access
Quartz, which records how long each run took
questions.explanation: The **Operations Mart** holds usage and performance data for reporting. It is the specific component created by the `pentaho_mart_postgresql.sql` script to track how content performs and is used.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Install Pentaho Server (Repository)

questions.scenario: After running the repository SQL scripts, an administrator finds no tables in the jackrabbit and hibuser databases. The administrator intends to rerun the scripts before starting the server.
questions.prompt: How should this situation be judged?
options: Start the server first: it creates those tables on first start
Drop and recreate both databases as the postgres user
Rerun the scripts: an empty schema means they failed
Restore the sample data, which creates the missing tables
questions.explanation:
The repository SQL scripts are only responsible for creating the databases and the necessary users. The **Pentaho Server** is responsible for creating the specific tables within the jackrabbit and hibuser databases upon its first startup.

Because the system is designed to generate these tables automatically during the initialization process, an empty schema is the expected state before the server is started.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Install Pentaho Server (Repository)

questions.scenario: The repository database moves to a new host. The administrator updates the connections in the Tomcat `context.xml` file only, and after a restart, the server fails when it reads repository content.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely reason?
options: Jackrabbit reads its connection from quartz.properties
A repository cannot be moved once it holds content
context.xml changes only take effect after a full reinstall
repository.xml still points Jackrabbit at the old host
questions.explanation: Quartz, Hibernate, Jackrabbit, and `context.xml` each carry connection details, and Jackrabbit's **repository.xml** points at the database directly, so all of them must agree on the new host and port.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Install Pentaho Server (Repository)

questions.scenario: An administrator copies a MySQL JDBC driver into the Tomcat `lib` folder to establish a new data connection, but the connection fails with a driver-not-found error.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely missing step?
options: Reboot the host so the operating system registers it
Restart the Pentaho Server so it loads the driver
Register the JAR in the License Manager
Copy the JAR into pentaho-solutions/system as well
questions.explanation: Tomcat loads the JAR files in its `lib` folder only at **startup**, so a driver copied in while the server runs is not seen until the server restarts.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Install Pentaho Server

questions.scenario: The Tomcat log shows the server started, but browsing to /pentaho returns an HTTP 404 error.
questions.prompt: Where should the administrator look first?
options: listen_addresses in postgresql.conf on the repository host
The Carte configuration, which is what serves the /pentaho path
Whether webapps/pentaho exists, and catalina's deployment errors
The License Manager, which hides /pentaho until a licence is added
questions.explanation: A 404 with Tomcat running means the **pentaho web app** did not deploy, so check that it is present under `webapps`, read Catalina's log for deployment errors, and check file permissions.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Install Pentaho Server

questions.scenario: A systemd unit runs start-pentaho.sh as root and lacks a restart configuration. A crash leaves the server down until a manual intervention occurs.
questions.prompt: Which settings fix both problems?
options: Group=root and TimeoutSec=0
User=pentaho and Restart=on-failure
Type=simple and RemainAfterExit=yes
User=root and Restart=always
questions.explanation: The `User=pentaho` setting ensures the server runs under an **unprivileged account** rather than as root. The `Restart=on-failure` setting ensures the systemd service **automatically restarts** the process following a crash.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Install Pentaho Server

questions.scenario: A server occasionally fails to locate its license because different user accounts and shells are used to start the service.
questions.prompt: What makes the license location consistent?
options: Entering the Activation ID again at each start
Copying the license file into every user's home folder
Storing the license inside Tomcat's server.xml
Setting PENTAHO_LICENSE_INFORMATION_PATH in /etc/environment
questions.explanation: Defining the **PENTAHO_LICENSE_INFORMATION_PATH** variable in the `/etc/environment` file ensures that the server identifies the correct location of the license file regardless of which user account or shell starts the service.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Install Pentaho Server

questions.scenario: An estate on Pentaho 9.3 is being upgraded, and the new licenses have arrived early. A colleague proposes starting the old server to activate them before the upgrade.
questions.prompt: How should that be judged?
options: Accept it: licenses must be active before any upgrade.
Reject it, because licenses can only be activated from the client tools.
Reject it: install the new version first, then activate the licenses.
Accept it, provided the old server is stopped straight after.
questions.explanation:
When upgrading from version 9.x or earlier, the **installation sequence** requires the new product version to be installed before the licenses are activated. The server must not be started before the licenses are upgraded; activating them on the old server first reverses the required order and cannot be corrected by stopping the old server afterward.

Licenses are activated specifically within the server's **License Manager**.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Install Pentaho Server

questions.scenario: Last year, the server's context path was changed from /pentaho to /company by renaming the web app and editing its files. Following an upgrade, users find that the /company links no longer function.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely cause?
options: The upgrade laid down the default web app, undoing the rename.
The upgrade deleted the repository's /company folder and its content.
The upgrade reset listen_addresses on the repository.
Context paths can no longer be changed after 10.x.
questions.explanation:
When an upgrade occurs, the system may replace the modified web application files with the default version. Because the custom **context path** was established by renaming and editing those specific files, any installation that overwrites the application will undo those changes.

To maintain a custom path through upgrades, the files must be reapplied or the path must be managed by a **reverse proxy**.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Post Installation Tasks

questions.scenario: Security requirements dictate that the Pentaho Server must serve HTTPS directly from a PKCS12 keystore without a reverse proxy.
questions.prompt: What does the administrator configure?
options: The keystore in Jackrabbit's repository.xml
An HTTPS switch in the User Console's administration settings
A keystore path entered in the License Manager
An SSL connector in server.xml pointing at the keystore
questions.explanation: The administrator configures an **SSL connector** in the `server.xml` file to enable HTTPS. This configuration requires the keystore type, file path, and password, while the `server.properties` file must be updated to reflect the correct scheme and port.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Post Installation Tasks

questions.scenario: A server is about to go live and still contains evaluation samples, including the sample content, the HSQL sample database, and a development-only status filter.
questions.prompt: What is the soundest approach?
options: Keep them, but hide the Public folder from ordinary users
Remove all of them before go-live, with the server stopped
Keep them, since removing the samples breaks the repository
Remove only the sample folders, through the User Console
questions.explanation: The **evaluation samples** (the sample content, the HSQL database definitions, and the `SystemStatusFilter` in `web.xml`) all come out before production, with the **server stopped** for the file changes. Removing them does not harm the repository.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Post Installation Tasks

questions.scenario: Security wants the login page to stop browsers from offering to remember passwords, and an administrator plans to edit the server's PUCLogin.jsp to implement this change.
questions.prompt: What is the drawback of that plan?
options: Editing the page requires the license to be activated again.
An upgrade can overwrite the vendor JSP and silently undo it.
The login page is served by Carte rather than by Tomcat.
A JSP edit needs the server recompiled from its source.
questions.explanation:
Modifying a vendor JSP file is unreliable because a system **upgrade** can overwrite the original file and silently undo the custom changes.

Because the original file is replaced during the update process, any local modifications are lost. Alternative methods, such as implementing controls at a **reverse proxy** or via single sign-on, are more persistent for security configurations.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Post Installation Tasks

questions.scenario: After a run of the Pentaho Upgrade Installer, the upgraded server starts cleanly, but two plugins it used before have gone.
questions.prompt: What explains it?
options: The upgrade does not keep plugins; they are reapplied from a backup.
They failed the installer's license check and were quarantined by it.
They come back by themselves after the first restart.
The installer moved them into the repository database.
questions.explanation: The upgrade process does not retain plugins during the installation; therefore, they are backed up to a separate directory before the process begins and are **reapplied from a backup** afterward. The same procedure applies to Hadoop cluster drivers.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Archive Installation — Pentaho Upgrade & Patches

questions.scenario: On an Ubuntu 24.04 workstation, `spoon.sh` fails at startup with errors about missing GTK and WebKit modules, though Java 21 is installed and PDI unpacked cleanly.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely fix?
options: Unpack PDI again with the jar tool instead of unzip
Run Spoon as root so that it can load the modules
Install the GTK and WebKit libraries Spoon's older UI needs
Point PENTAHO_JAVA_HOME at a Java 11 runtime, which bundles them
questions.explanation: Some of Spoon's legacy UI depends on **GTK and WebKit libraries** that vary by desktop, and Ubuntu 24.04 does not ship the ones it expects, so installing them fixes the start.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Install Client Tools — Client Plugins

questions.scenario: On a high-DPI laptop, Spoon's toolbars and dialogs render too small to read.
questions.prompt: What is a quick way to fix the scaling?
options: Start Spoon with GDK_SCALE=2 set
Reinstall PDI with the Evaluation Wizard
Point PENTAHO_JAVA_HOME at a HiDPI runtime
Pass -Xmx2g in Spoon's startup script
questions.explanation: Spoon's interface is drawn through GTK on Linux, and setting **GDK_SCALE** to 2 doubles its scale. Adjusting the desktop's own scaling works too.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Install Client Tools — Client Plugins

questions.scenario: Designers report Spoon slowing to a crawl and then failing with out-of-memory errors while they preview large transformations.
questions.prompt: What should be adjusted?
options: shared_buffers on the repository's PostgreSQL
The -Xms and -Xmx heap settings in Spoon's startup script
Spoon's log level, set lower for each large transformation
The Pentaho Server's session timeout in web.xml
questions.explanation: Out-of-memory errors in a client tool indicate that the **JVM heap** is too small to process the data. Increasing the `-Xms` and `-Xmx` values in the startup script provides the application with more available memory for execution.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Install Client Tools — Client Plugins

questions.scenario: Production is certified against an earlier version of a PDI plugin, and a developer's workstation must match that specific version rather than the latest available version.
questions.prompt: What is the correct way to install the specific version?
options: Install the latest, since the Plugin Manager cannot pin versions.
Copy the older JAR into the plugins folder by hand instead.
Install the latest, then edit the version number in its JAR.
Open the plugin's row in the Plugin Manager and pick that version.
questions.explanation:
The **Plugin Manager** allows for the installation of specific versions of a plugin by selecting the desired version from the options provided in the plugin's row.

This method ensures that the local environment remains consistent with the certified production environment while allowing the manager to continue handling updates and removals.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Install Client Tools — Kettle Plugins

questions.scenario: A team must upsert millions of records into Salesforce from PDI and route the records that fail into a separate error table.
questions.prompt: Which plugin step fits this?
options: Hierarchical Data Type, which bulk-loads nested records into Salesforce
Google Analytics v4, which writes the records to Salesforce objects
Bulk load into Databricks, which runs COPY INTO against Salesforce
Salesforce Bulk Operation, which routes failures to their own stream
questions.explanation: The **Salesforce Bulk Operation** step performs insert, update, upsert, and delete operations through the Bulk API 2.0. It is designed to handle large volumes of data and can route successful, unprocessed, and failed records to separate streams when provided with a Client ID and Secret.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Install Client Tools — Kettle Plugins

questions.scenario: On a designer's workstation, Spoon starts but its enterprise features are disabled and it prompts for a license, while the server's licenses are all active.
questions.prompt: What should be checked first?
options: That the workstation runs Ubuntu 24.04 rather than another OS
That Spoon was unpacked with unzip rather than with jar
That the server has been restarted since its license was added
That client entitlements are activated and the license path is set
questions.explanation: Client tools require their own **entitlements** to be activated in the License Manager. Additionally, the `PENTAHO_LICENSE_INFORMATION_PATH` environment variable must be correctly configured to point to the location of the license file for that specific user.
questions.source: Pentaho Installation - Practitioner: Install Client Tools — Client Plugins
